newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Danish long yields up to 7.27 pct end-97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Danish long yields up to 7.27 pct end-97.

text.p: Danish bond yields have bottomed out and will climb steadily over the next 12 months, according to a Reuter consensus poll of 21 economists.
An average of forecasts shows the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006, currently yielding around 6.60 percent, rising to 7.27 pct by the end of 1997.

By end-March 1997 the benchmark was seen yielding 6.92 percent, rising to an average 7.14 percent by end-June 1997. The 10-year yield gap with Germany was expected on average to widen from around 80 basis points today to 90 b.p. in March and June, narrowing to 87 b.p. again in 12 months.

Three-month rates would rise from 3.60 percent now to an average 3.62 percent in three months, rising to 3.79 percent in six months and 4.13 percent next December, the poll said. --Kenneth Lund Pedersen +45 33969650
